panelCountDefinition: Items with type 3 (KqlItem), including KqlItems nested in upstream NotebookGroup items.

panels.mapping: ZPAEvent open sessions grouped by SrcGeoCountry -> allowed _Im_NetworkSession rows grouped by SrcGeoCountry
Raw DvcAction distribution -> normalized DvcAction distribution
ZPA event count series -> ZPA-filtered Network Session count series
Open-session source IP counts -> allowed-session source IP counts
Raw close rows grouped by raw EventResult -> End rows grouped by original result detail or vendor close-reason fallback
Raw UrlHostname counts -> normalized destination FQDN counts
Traffic and trend by raw DstUserName -> normalized SrcUsername; SrcBytes remains SrcBytes
New source IP for a user; target uses a non-overlapping baseline and a leftanti join keyed by user and IP
SecurityAlert VPN rows -> SecurityAlert rows precisely scoped to Zscaler and ZPA/VPN alert identity

limitations: SecurityAlert is used only by Latest Alerts because that panel displays Sentinel-derived alerts rather than raw Zscaler telemetry. Its filter requires a Zscaler alert name plus a ZPA/VPN alert-name indicator or a Zscaler Private Access description.
Normalized DvcAction values are not raw ZPA open/close values: open maps to Allow and close maps to EventSubType End.
Connection-close reason parity depends on EventOriginalResultDetails or AdditionalFields.ConnectionCloseReason being populated by the ingestion pipeline.
DstFQDN preserves hostname semantics but not a URL scheme/path that might have existed in raw UrlHostname.

The New VPN Users upstream query mixes the current interval into its baseline and drops the user join key. The target corrects this so the panel can actually identify a source IP not seen for that same user in the preceding baseline.
The upstream Top VPN Traffic query orders Traffic(MB) ascending before take 8 despite its title. That behavior is preserved rather than silently changing the ranked population.
